paper_metadata.title: Room and high-temperature tensile properties of austenitic stainless steel 321 fabricated by wire arc additive manufacturing
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

evidence.quote: SS 321 is a potential structural alloy for elevated temperature applications. In this work, austenitic stainless steel 321 (SS 321) was successfully fabricated via wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM).
The wrought SS 321 consists of equiaxed grains along with a small amount of ferrite ( < 0.5 FN), and TiC [ 17 , 21 ] is noticed within the dominant austenitic matrix as shown in Fig. 3 b.
This study evaluated the microstructure and the relative mechanical properties of wrought SS 321 and WAAM 321 from RT to 900 ◦C.

Quasi-static tensile tests were carried out at room temperature (RT) and elevated temperatures (300 °C, 600 °C, and 900 °C) with micro tensile specimens extracted from the wrought plate (SS 321-BM) and WAAM 321 wall at horizontal (WAAM 321-H, parallel to deposition direction) and vertical (WAAM 321-V, parallel to build direction-BD) orientations.
The wrought SS 321 consists of equiaxed grains along with a small amount of ferrite ( < 0.5 FN), and TiC [ 17 , 21 ] is noticed within the dominant austenitic matrix as shown in Fig. 3 b.
Fig. 3 a shows the macrostructure of the WAAM 321 wall component, devoid of defects such as cracks, fissures, and pores.
At 900 ◦ C, the YS, UTS, and EL of SS 321-BM are 95 ± 5 MPa, 108 ± 6 MPa, and 67 ± 3.5 %, respectively.
The WAAM 321-H specimens have better YS and UTS than the WAAM 321-V specimens. The WAAM 321-V specimen has 6 – 7 layers compared to the WAAM 321-H specimens with 2 – 3 layers.
The WAAM 321-V specimen has 6 – 7 layers compared to the WAAM 321-H specimens with 2 – 3 layers.
The as-printed WAAM 321 wall was free from defects, and the complex thermal history influenced the ferrite fraction along the BD.
The wrought SS 321-BM has a dominant austenitic phase with a small fraction of ferrite, while the residual delta ferrite in WAAM 321 ranged between 3.6 and 5.9 FN along the BD.

An OTC Daihen FD-B6 robotic welding system connected with Welbee P500L power source was employed to build the wall having dimensions of 80 × 8 × 150 mm (length × width × height) followed by slicing of edges and face-milling for preparing specimens shown in Fig. 1. WAAM process variables optimized from trial and error experiments were used, including the welding current of 140 Amps, welding speed of 180 mm/min, and arc voltage of 16.2 V. The 98 % Argon and 2 % Carbon dioxide gas mixture was supplied at 20 L/min to protect the molten pool during deposition.
Subsequently, the specimens for microstructural analysis and tensile tests were prepared using wire electric discharge machining.
